title: A lot of vram remains occupied after T2V run
body: After the first run of the T2V workflow a lot of memory remains occupied. It can be freed manually using the "Free model and node cache" functionality.  If that one is not used, my second run struggles with low vram and starts using shared memory. The size of the memory occupancy seems to correspond with the latents of the previous run, so maybe the latents output from the sampler are staying in vram?

comments.body: The latents would only be couple of megabytes, is this with block swapping? Perhaps part of the model stays in VRAM.

There's no block swapping enabled as I'm just using the tiny 1.3B model. Occupancy while inferencing is ~65%, post-completion it stays at 55% and on the next run it goes to 95% + shared memory. 10GB vram and 768x768x81.

I was watching it complete live just now, and noticed that the vram did drop to ~11% after the sampler finished, but then pushed up to 95% when doing the vae decoding. It reduced to 52% after decoding was completed, but no further. Some sort of decoding cache not being emptied?

I think I found it, there's some caching in the VAE that's not cleared, I could replicate this with simply loading VAE and encoding something, it would use ~2GB VRAM no matter what I did. There was a function already in the VAE to clear it, so just calling it frees it all. 

Thanks for raising the issue, this was a lot of wasted VRAM even for normal inference.

satisfaction_conditions: Identification of the root cause of VRAM remaining occupied after T2V runs
Confirmation that the issue can be fixed
Explanation of why memory usage increases on subsequent runs

_classification.category: Requires build environment but hard to be dockerized
